trigger: operator has (or creates) a result-set `name` used as an alias >64 bytes (up to the 256-byte kResultSetNameMaxLen ceiling), then references it as `parent_id` on from-tar-query or from-instruction-result (REST, via the shared run_async->resolve_owned_parent->resolve_alias path)
summary: The new 64-byte kResultSetParentIdMaxLen length-cap check runs BEFORE resolve_owned_parent/resolve_alias, so a real, previously-valid 65-256 byte alias now 400s before alias resolution is even attempted. Pre-existing on MCP's identical producer tools (mcp_server.cpp, #4353); this diff extends the same cap to REST for parity, which is where the previously-working call regresses (REST had no length bound on parent_id at all before this diff). Independently confirmed by architect (sharpened: 'a regression on valid input, not just a 404 narrowing'), dsl-engineer, unhappy-path (UP-1), consistency-auditor (C-4: changelog omits it), enterprise-readiness (confirmed via direct call-path trace: only 2 of 4 routes affected, since the other 2 never resolve aliases).
classification_rationale: the #4734 changelog.d fragment does not mention this behavioural change (required-doc item 3); a missing changelog note for a Breaking-shaped behaviour change is an absence, not wording

adjudication_rationale: compliance-officer's POLICY FLOOR classification does not meet the closed three-source list in the shared severity preamble (routed-concerns row clause / CLAUDE.md standing-rule sentence / accepted ADR). docs/observability-conventions.md is a routed DOC, not itself one of the three sources, and the routed-concerns.md row pointing to it carries no inline catastrophic-if-violated clause. De-escalated from POLICY FLOOR to derived SHOULD band; the underlying finding is not disputed and is fixed in the Gate 7 round regardless.
trigger: a caller sends an oversized (>64 byte) parent_id to any of the 3 REST length-cap call sites (generic create, run_async covering from-tar-query/from-instruction-result, from-inventory-query)
summary: REST's 3 new parent_id length-cap rejections call bare rs_err(res,400,...) with no audit_fn call and no metric increment, while MCP's identical rejection (reject_field_too_large) fires both mcp_audit('denied',...) and increments yuzu_mcp_tool_args_too_large_total. Intra-route inconsistency also present: the malformed/empty-parent_id guard 3-20 lines away on the SAME route/action DOES call audit_fn. sre and compliance-officer both independently re-derived MEDIUM-or-below on this same fact (shown as context). compliance-officer additionally classified this a POLICY FLOOR citing docs/observability-conventions.md:125's 'Denied operations MUST emit an audit event' sentence -- ADJUDICATED (by workflow-orchestrator + advisor consult) that this does NOT meet the closed floor-source list (a catastrophic-if-violated clause embedded in a routed-concerns row itself, a CLAUDE.md standing-rule sentence, or an accepted ADR): the observability row in .claude/routed-concerns.md carries no such clause inline and merely points to the doc ('Gate mechanics and their limits are in the routed doc'); docs/observability-conventions.md is itself none of the three closed sources. Recorded at its derived band (SHOULD), not as a floor. Fixed regardless via the same Gate 7 fix round the finding recommends, so floor-membership was not load-bearing to the disposition.
classification_rationale: not a doc/prose finding; classification field used loosely here to satisfy schema -- see summary for the floor-adjudication note

trigger: a caller supplies device_ids with an oversized individual entry, or a foreign parent_id alongside a genuinely oversized device_ids array, on the generic REST create_result_set route
summary: REST's generic create route has NO per-entry device_ids length bound at all (MCP's twin enforces kResultSetDeviceIdMaxLen), and REST's kMaxMembersPerSet count check still runs AFTER load_owned while MCP's runs before -- so {parent_id: <foreign>, device_ids: [<oversized>]} 404s on REST before the field-too-large problem is reported, while MCP reports it regardless of parent ownership. Pre-existing, not touched by this diff's device_ids handling -- but the new code's own 'mirroring MCP's twin' comment invites the comparison. Out of this PR's accepted scope (device_ids validation, not parent_id/limit). NOTE: reporter (consistency-auditor) prose stated IMPACT I2/I4; corrected by the recorder (workflow-orchestrator) to I6 on review -- an unbounded string length is not data corruption (I2) and involves no operator-facing guidance (I4); the defect is a missing/misordered validation bound, which is I6 (capability/consistency gap), consistent with the SHOULD band both the reporter and this ledger assign.
classification_rationale: not a doc finding; a genuine pre-existing validation-ordering/completeness gap surfaced while reviewing this diff's own parity claim

trigger: a caller sends a non-numeric limit query-string value to GET /api/v1/result-sets or GET /api/v1/result-sets/{id}/members
summary: This PR makes MCP's list_result_sets/get_result_set_members strict on limit, but REST's documented twins still use std::from_chars and silently fall back to default on any non-numeric value. Pre-PR both transports were symmetrically loose; post-PR MCP is strict and REST stays loose for the identical logical parameter -- a REST/MCP asymmetry this diff widens without touching REST. Out of this PR's accepted scope (query-string params have no 'wrong JSON type' failure mode the way JSON-RPC args do, so the fix shape would differ).
classification_rationale: not a doc finding -- cross-transport parity gap

classification_rationale: not a doc finding -- architectural refactor suggestion
